# Juniper (Junos) MIB Reference — EX/QFX Series Switches

Read [00-architecture/standard-mibs.md](../../00-architecture/standard-mibs.md) first — this file only documents what Junos adds, restricts, or does differently on top of that shared baseline. Raw MIB text is **not vendored** for Juniper (see [overview.md](overview.md#mib-licensingredistribution-note--why-mibs-is-link-only-for-juniper) and [mibs/README.md](mibs/README.md)); OIDs below are sourced from Juniper's own documentation pages, cross-checked against the LibreNMS/Observium mirrors where noted, without redistributing those files.

## Standard MIBs Junos supports, and quirks

Per [SNMP MIBs Supported by Junos OS and Junos OS Evolved](https://www.juniper.net/documentation/us/en/software/junos/network-mgmt/topics/topic-map/snmp-mibs-supported-by-junos-os-and-junos-os-evolved.html):

| MIB | Junos support | Quirks |
|---|---|---|
| SNMPv2-MIB | Yes | Standard `system` group; used the same way as any other vendor for identification (`sysObjectID` under the Juniper enterprise arc `1.3.6.1.4.1.2636`). |
| IF-MIB (RFC 2863) | Yes, plus RFC 2864 Inverted Stack Table extension | `ifTable`/`ifXTable` present as usual. **`ifAdminStatus` (`.1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.7`) is explicitly documented as not SET-able on Junos** — see "SNMP write support" below. This is the single biggest practical difference from other vendors' IF-MIB behavior. |
| BRIDGE-MIB (RFC 1286 base; RFC 4188 not explicitly listed, RFC 4318 RSTP extension present) | Yes | Junos's supported-MIBs page cites the older RFC 1286 "Definitions of Managed Objects for Bridges" plus the RFC 4318 RSTP MIB extension explicitly — confirm the exact `dot1dStp`-vs-RSTP-extension object availability against [MIB Explorer](https://apps.juniper.net/mib-explorer/) for the specific EX/QFX model and release rather than assuming full RFC 4188 parity. |
| Q-BRIDGE-MIB (RFC 4363) | Yes | Read path (`dot1qVlanStaticTable`, `dot1qVlanCurrentTable`, `dot1qPvid`) is generally reliable for VLAN read-back/polling. **SNMP SET-driven VLAN creation via `dot1qVlanStaticRowStatus` is not confirmed as supported/reliable on EX series** — field reports on the `juniper-nsp` mailing list discuss inconsistent NMS support of Junos VLAN MIBs, and Junos ELS-style platforms are reported to implement Q-BRIDGE-MIB differently from non-ELS platforms. Treat as **read-only in practice** unless verified against the specific target platform/release. ([j-nsp: SNMP NMS support of Junos VLAN MIBs](https://puck.nether.net/pipermail/juniper-nsp/2016-November/033724.html)) |
| LLDP-MIB (IEEE 802.1AB) | Yes, explicitly listed | Standard neighbor-discovery read path, same as other vendors. |
| ENTITY-MIB | Junos lists **RFC 4133** support (not the newer RFC 6933 that `standard-mibs.md` documents as the cross-vendor baseline) | `entPhysicalTable` should still be readable for chassis/module/PSU/fan inventory, but confirm exact object availability (e.g. some RFC 6933-only augmentations may be absent) against MIB Explorer per platform. |
| RMON-MIB (RFC 2819) | Yes, plus Juniper's own extensions (`mib-jnx-rmon` — "RMON Events and Alarms MIB") | Juniper documents an enterprise extension augmenting the standard alarm table rather than relying solely on RFC 2819 objects. |
| Host Resources MIB (RFC 2790) | Also listed | Not part of SignalScope's cross-vendor baseline set, but available if CPU/memory-style polling needs it — note per [connectivity-methods.md](../../00-architecture/connectivity-methods.md), CPU/memory exposure via SNMP is inconsistent across vendors generally; verify Host Resources MIB actually reports switch-plane CPU/memory (as opposed to just RE/control-plane values) before relying on it. |

Not explicitly confirmed as present in the supported-MIBs listing we reviewed: a dedicated standalone "BRIDGE-MIB (RFC 4188)" citation — Junos's own page cites RFC 1286 + RFC 4318 rather than RFC 4188 by name. Treat the exact classic-STP (`dot1dStp`) object-level behavior as "confirm against MIB Explorer for the target platform," not assumed identical to a full RFC 4188 implementation.

## Juniper enterprise MIBs relevant to switch management

Rooted under the Juniper private enterprise arc `1.3.6.1.4.1.2636` (`juniperMIB`), organized under `jnxMibs` (`1.3.6.1.4.1.2636.3`). Per [Enterprise-Specific MIBs Overview](https://www.juniper.net/documentation/en_US/junos/topics/concept/enterprise-specific-mibs-overview.html):

| MIB | Purpose | OID (confirmed vs. uncertain) |
|---|---|---|
| **JUNIPER-MIB** (`jnxBoxAnatomy`, the "Chassis MIB") | Environmental monitoring and hardware inventory (temperature, fans, PSUs, FRU status/traps like `jnxFruFailed`/`jnxFruOffline`/`jnxFruOnline`). | Rooted at `jnxMibs 1` = `1.3.6.1.4.1.2636.3.1` — **confirmed**, read directly from the module's own `::= { jnxMibs 1 }` clause in the MIB text. |
| **JUNIPER-CHASSIS-DEFINES-MIB** (`jnxChassisDefines`) | TEXTUAL-CONVENTION definitions (chassis IDs, FRU types) imported by JUNIPER-MIB; supporting/enumeration MIB rather than a queryable object tree of its own. | `1.3.6.1.4.1.2636.3.25` (`jnxChassisDefines`) — **confirmed** via `oidref.com` cross-check, not independently verified against Juniper's own MIB text in this pass; treat as high-confidence but not first-party-confirmed. |
| **JUNIPER-VLAN-MIB** (`mib-jnx-vlan`) | VLAN objects, including the Juniper-specific VLAN tag object (`jnxExVlanTag`) needed alongside Q-BRIDGE-MIB to get full VLAN-tag-to-port mapping on some platforms. Juniper's own overview page describes it as covering "pre-standard IEEE 802.1Q VLANs." | Root path components (`jnxMibs.jnxExMibRoot.jnxExSwitching.jnxExVlan.jnxVlanMIBObjects`) resolve to **`1.3.6.1.4.1.2636.3.40.1.5.1`** per third-party OID lookup (`oidref.com`) — **not independently confirmed against Juniper's own MIB text in this pass; treat the exact numeric path as unconfirmed** and verify against MIB Explorer before hardcoding. Also reported unsupported/inconsistent on Junos ELS platforms — see LLDP/Q-BRIDGE note above. |
| **JUNIPER-L2ALD-MIB** (`mib-jnx-l2ald`) | Layer 2 Address Learning Daemon MIB — VLAN/MAC-learning info via `jnxL2aldVlanTable`; reported as the MIB that works across **both** EX and QFX (vs. JUNIPER-VLAN-MIB, which is reported EX-non-ELS-only). | Numeric OID **not confirmed** in this pass — treat as "exists, exact path unverified." |
| **JUNIPER-CFGMGMT-MIB** ("JUNIPER-CONFIG-MANAGEMENT-MIB" in some secondary sources; Juniper's own naming is `mib-jnx-cfgmgmt`) | Configuration-change **notifications only** — traps for configuration changes and rescue-configuration changes, with a change-history table (`jnxCmChgEventTable`). **This is a notification/audit MIB, not a configuration-write MIB.** | Root `jnxCfgMgmt` = `1.3.6.1.4.1.2636.3.18` — **confirmed** via a specific object (`jnxCmCfgChgLatestTime` = `1.3.6.1.4.1.2636.3.18.1.2`) found directly in Juniper's own doc reference for that object; the parent root OID itself is inferred from that child path, not independently re-derived, so treat as high-confidence rather than fully first-party-verified. |
| **Fabric Chassis MIB** (`mib-jnx-fabric-chassis`) | Extension of the chassis MIB for QFabric-style multi-device fabric systems; not relevant to standalone EX/QFX switches. | N/A for this doc's scope. |

**Nothing in the researched Juniper enterprise MIB set documents general SNMP-writable switch-port configuration** (no enterprise equivalent of "write a VLAN/port-security/STP config object"). JUNIPER-CFGMGMT-MIB in particular is easy to mistake for a config-write MIB from its name alone — it is **not**; it only emits notifications *about* config changes made some other way (CLI/NETCONF), and exposes a read-only history table.

## SNMP write support — the honest summary

Because of the candidate-config/commit model described in [overview.md](overview.md), and because Junos's own SNMP FAQ explicitly disallows `ifAdminStatus` SET, **SNMP SET-driven configuration changes on Junos are unusual and narrow compared to Cisco-family devices**:

- Confirmed writable via SNMP SET (with a `read-write` community/view configured): `snmpCommunityTable` entries, RMON `eventTable`/`alarmTable` rows, and basic system scalars (`sysContact.0`, `sysName.0`, `sysLocation.0`). ([Junos OS SNMP FAQs](https://www.juniper.net/documentation/us/en/software/junos/network-mgmt/topics/topic-map/junos-os-snmp-faqs.html))
- Confirmed **not** writable: `IF-MIB::ifAdminStatus` (explicit FAQ statement, corroborated by a Juniper community report of the same symptom).
- Not confirmed either way in this research pass, and not recommended to assume: `Q-BRIDGE-MIB::dot1qVlanStaticRowStatus`-driven VLAN creation (mixed field reports, ELS-platform inconsistency); any enterprise-MIB config-write path (none found).
- **Real Junos automation for configuration changes uses NETCONF** (the `Junos XML Protocol` / NETCONF-over-SSH interface, port 830), which operates directly against the same candidate-configuration/commit model as the CLI — not a bypass of it. This is *why* SNMP write support stayed narrow on Junos: Juniper built a purpose-designed transactional config protocol instead of extending SNMP SET coverage. ([Junos NETCONF XML Management Protocol Developer Guide](https://www.juniper.net/documentation/us/en/software/junos/netconf/netconf.pdf))

**Practical conclusion for SignalScope**: for Junos devices, do not build any GUI action whose only implementation path is an SNMP SET against a switch-config object — with the possible narrow exception of the confirmed-writable objects listed above (none of which cover port/VLAN/STP/LACP/port-security config). Every config-changing GUI action for Junos must route through a live CLI session (or, as a longer-term option outside this research phase's CLI/SNMP-only scope, NETCONF) ending in an explicit `commit`. SNMP's role for Junos devices in SignalScope is **read-only telemetry and inventory polling**, not a control-plane fallback.
